title: Israeli Strike on Gaza City Seaport Cafe Kills Six, Including a Child
detail: An Israeli airstrike hit a crowded cafe at Gaza City's port on August 18, 2026, killing at least six people, including a child, and wounding 14 others. The strike hit as displaced people sheltering at the port — now a makeshift displacement camp — came out of their tents to escape extreme heat. The IDF claimed the strike, calling it a 'precise aerial strike' that targeted a gathering of several Hamas commanders and members of the Nukhba Force elite unit that led the October 7, 2023 invasion, but provided no evidence. Hamas denounced the strike as a 'blatant disregard for all calls for a ceasefire issued by mediators and guarantor states.' The strike came a day after US envoy Jared Kushner concluded an unsuccessful regional visit aimed at advancing the 15-point Gaza peace plan, with both Hamas and Netanyahu refusing to budge on their core demands.

title: Uganda and Burundi Military Officers Conduct Pre-Deployment Site Survey in Rafah
detail: Senior military officers from Uganda and Burundi visited Rafah in southern Gaza on August 18, 2026 for a 'pre-deployment site survey' amid preliminary talks with the Israeli defense establishment about contributing troops to the planned International Stabilization Force (ISF). The visit followed talks at the US-led Civil-Military Coordination Center in Kiryat Gat. Uganda had already announced approval to deploy troops under the Board of Peace's 20-point postwar plan; Burundi was at a more preliminary discussion stage. An Israeli security source told Channel 12 that, 'against the backdrop of the political situation, we do not expect any progress toward an agreement in the Gaza Strip,' with officials not anticipating a dramatic move on Gaza before Israel's October 27 elections.
